value.rationale: The quartic Lamé oval is the simplest analytic smooth strictly convex plane oval with canonical isolated quadratic curvature zeros. The known 2/3 boundary-triangle law becomes nonintegrable there; a distinct 3/5 probability exponent and a new exact constant and marked total-variation limit explain the geometry of exceptional tiny triangles and are not an arbitrary numerical slice.
